summary: Republican Byron Donalds holds a huge money edge and the backing of Trump and DeSantis, while CBS Miami reported in early October that polls ranged from a clear Donalds lead to a tie or a Jolly edge. The race has centered on home insurance costs, affordability and school funding, with no debates after the two sides failed to agree on terms.

issues.why: Jolly wants a state fund to cover all wind risk while Donalds wants to keep the Cat Fund as a reinsurer and protect the 2022 lawsuit limits.
Donalds says Jolly would raise taxes and costs, while Jolly ties rising gas, grocery and insurance prices to Trump and Donalds.
Jolly proposes moving tourism tax dollars toward classrooms, while Donalds argues current policies fueled the state's growth.
Donalds says Jolly lobbied for offshore drilling in 2011 and fact checkers found the claim technically true, while Donalds' stance on AI data centers has shifted.

storylines.title: Obama backs Jolly
storylines.what: Former President Barack Obama endorsed Jolly as Trump stepped up his involvement in Florida.

storylines.title: Jolly ad ties Donalds to Trump
storylines.what: A Jolly ad called Daddy's Back argues that gas, grocery and insurance costs rose under Trump and that Donalds shows Trump blind loyalty.

storylines.title: Fact checks hit both sides
storylines.what: WUFT found Jolly's claim of 60 to 70 percent premium cuts likely false and Donalds' $1,000 hurricane tax figure not correct as stated.

storylines.title: Donalds launches Fighter and Never ads
storylines.what: Donalds aired an ad featuring Trump's praise and another arguing Jolly would raise taxes and insurance costs, backed by a fundraising haul of over $134 million.

storylines.title: Insurance plans collide
storylines.what: Donalds calls Jolly's state wind fund socialism, while Jolly says the current system already imposes a hurricane tax on Citizens policyholders.

storylines.title: Dueling tours on the Suncoast
storylines.what: Donalds praised Republican leadership on his Defending the Florida Dream tour while Jolly met with the Sarasota school board about education funding.

storylines.title: FAMU debate canceled
storylines.what: Florida A&M canceled a planned gubernatorial debate after the campaigns could not agree.

storylines.title: Jolly says no to debates
storylines.what: Jolly's campaign said he would not debate, arguing the Donalds camp tried to control the moderator, location and timing, and each side blamed the other.

events.title: Hurricane tax attack
events.prompt: The two campaigns are trading charges over home insurance, with Republicans calling a state wind fund a hurricane tax and Democrats saying Citizens surcharges already are one. How does the campaign answer on insurance?

opts.label: State wind fund
opts.say: Back a public fund that covers all wind risk so private premiums fall.

opts.label: Scorecard and grants
opts.say: Keep the current market but add a consumer insurance scorecard and fix the home hardening grants.

opts.label: Defend 2022 reforms
opts.say: Protect the lawsuit limits, keep Citizens small and call any state takeover socialism.

events.title: Debate standoff
events.prompt: Talks on three televised debates broke down over moderators, venues and dates, and a FAMU debate was canceled. What does the campaign do?

opts.label: Accept any debate
opts.say: Publicly accept any neutral debate offer and dare the other side to show up.

opts.label: Town halls instead
opts.say: Skip debates and hold separate televised town halls with voters.

opts.label: Blame and move on
opts.say: Say the other side sabotaged the talks and focus on paid ads.

events.title: Trump and rising prices
events.prompt: A new ad argues gas, groceries and insurance costs rose under Trump and that the Republican nominee gave him an A on the economy. How does the campaign handle Trump on cost of living?

opts.label: Blame Trump
opts.say: Say Trump's tariffs and the Iran war raised prices and Floridians are paying the bill.

opts.label: Talk state costs
opts.say: Stay on state level fixes for insurance and housing and avoid national fights.

opts.label: Embrace Trump
opts.say: Run on Trump's endorsement and the tax cut bill as proof of results.

events.title: Schools and tourist taxes
events.prompt: A proposal to move tourism tax dollars from convention centers and promotion to public schools is drawing attention. Where does the campaign land?

opts.label: Shift to classrooms
opts.say: Redirect tourist tax money to teacher pay and classrooms.

opts.label: Local choice
opts.say: Let counties decide how to spend their own tourist tax revenue.

opts.label: Keep the model
opts.say: Say low taxes and school choice built Florida and the current system works.

ads.theme: The Never ad argues liberal David Jolly would raise taxes, insurance and everyday costs.
The Fighter ad features Trump praising Donalds.
An ad claims Jolly's insurance plan is a $1,000 a year hurricane tax, a figure fact checkers dispute.
The Daddy's Back ad says prices rose under Trump and Donalds gives him blind loyalty.

regions.name: South Florida
regions.note: The Democratic base in Broward and Palm Beach, while Miami-Dade's Hispanic voters swung sharply right in recent cycles.

regions.name: I-4 corridor and Orlando
regions.note: Orange and Osceola lean Democratic with large Puerto Rican communities, while the surrounding suburbs and Space Coast lean Republican.

regions.name: Tampa Bay
regions.note: Jolly's home turf in Pinellas, a historic swing area that has drifted Republican.

regions.name: Southwest Florida and Suncoast
regions.note: Donalds' home base around Naples and Fort Myers, heavily Republican with many retirees.

regions.name: North Florida and Panhandle
regions.note: Deep red rural and military areas, offset by Democratic Tallahassee, Gainesville and a competitive Jacksonville.
